text: The fee calculation has no command of its own: it is a step of InstructionWorkflow on task queue rwb-partner, started by the payment of a case placed with an agency, and the result is read back on the two published reads the legacy story names, GET /partner/instructions (API-S9-003) and GET /partners (API-S9-001) on /api/recovery/partner/v1 with the Partner portal right R; whether the trigger is an event-started workflow or a Temporal Schedule is left to the app story, and no second path and no write operation is declared.
why: FSD S9 A2.7.2 gives the trigger as a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer with the system as actor and no user step, FSD S9 A2.7.3.3 gives None; runs unattended as the primary role, the legacy permission table gives the Partner portal right R only, and the legacy Endpoints table names exactly the two reads. Declaring a fee command would invent an operation the sources do not have, and leaving the read back open would leave the fee invisible.

applied_in: RWB-S9-E6035-APP sections 1, 2, 4, 7, 8 BR8, 12.1, 12.5, 12.6 and 13; RWB-S9-E6035-CON sections 2, 3, 7 AC1, 8 BR7 and BR12, 12.1 and 12.6

impact: The fee rides the published reads and the service's own workflow, a build that adds a fee command or a second path fails the review, and the trigger's delivery is settled by the app story

text: The money recovered by the agency is read from rwb-payment on a REST consumed row, because the legacy story and FSD S9 name FEAT-PAY-01 as the prerequisite and ALS and GL as the integration point while the legacy Data table carries no payment entity, and the case is read from rwb-case; neither fact is copied into rwb_partner, whose own tables hold the instruction and its result code only.
why: Template and Rules v1 R3 ranks the module TSD and FSD above the story master and neither gives S9 a payment table, while the context pack's ownership rows give S9 three tables (partner, partner_instruction, partner_user) and no payment. Reading an ACE table or a v_ace_* view would break DP-05, and inventing a payment table would give this service a fact another owner holds.

text: The fee due is worked out from the contracted fee schedule read as versioned reference data, and it is accrued on partner_instruction.fee_amount (DF-PRT-016), the only fee field any source publishes; the schedule's columns, its rate basis, its tiers, its rounding and its effective dates are Not specified in the source documents, so they carry the placeholder and no column, table or enumeration is added, and the fee properties of the answer carry the same placeholder.
why: FEAT-PRM-02 promises the panel and fee schedule as versioned reference data and REQ-S9-004 says fees are calculated from the contracted schedule, but TSD S9 T3.1 lists no schedule table and no rate, the FSD omits A2.7.3.2 (the field catalog), and TSD S9 T3.2 publishes no fee list. Writing a percentage or a basis into the code would be a business value, and adding a column would invent a schema the DB story does not hold.
